reason: The entry tree, reconciliation and write-back already exist in src/go/loader; the design adds intercept, full validation with source positions, an expression seam and a mutation API to it.
File binding, patches and the journal are replaced by a codec seam, first-class layer composition with one writable layer, and the existing snapshot three-way merge refined to fields.
The package is a three-line re-export of the loader's Group plugin; in Go a group is a kind of entry inside the loader with children, inject and isolate, not a separate plugin.
Config reload is kept through the loader's watched layer source; in-process code reload is impossible for compiled-in components and becomes a restart of the entry that owns a plugin process.
The Go cordis logger already has console and slog exporters; a harness logging component configures them, and the cosmetic formatting options are not carried over.
src/go/timer already provides fiber-owned timeout, interval, sleep, throttle and debounce with tests, and the design uses it unchanged.
The deprecated setTimeout alias is not part of the Go timer, which has one name per operation (Timeout).
The deprecated setInterval alias is not part of the Go timer, which has one name per operation (Interval).
The FIXME marks the unmerged inject-mapping config; in Go an entry's inject is a list of names only and per-service config uses intercept, read in a fixed layer order, so nothing needs merging.

title: Config files run arbitrary JavaScript (!!js through eval inside with(ctx)) with the full authority of the host process

reason: Expressions become side-effect-free data reads in a restricted language with a fixed set of names, checked at parse time; no code from a config file runs in the host.

title: Code hot reload depends on Node's private module loader (expose-internals or a native addon) and tracks two incompatible internal API shapes

reason: The dependency exists only because Node has no public module-cache API; Go components are compiled in and code is never replaced in process.

title: The loader writes a .cordis/resolve.mjs helper and a .gitignore into the user's project to resolve modules there

reason: The helper exists only because of Node ESM module resolution; the Go loader resolves component names in a table registered at compile time.

title: A runtime write-back serialises parsed data instead of the parsed document, so comments and layout of a hand-edited config file are lost

reason: The YAML codec applies runtime changes to the kept node tree and re-encodes it, so comments on untouched nodes survive a write.
